task_brief: This is day 3 of "Computing Systems, Files, and Troubleshooting". That is unit 2 in grade 5. Today is a guided practice about files and folders. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Organize a sample project folder and write a step-by-step troubleshooting flowchart. Today helps by working on files and folders. Your unit also covers hardware and software, input output storage, files and folders, and naming and versions. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Do two problems about files and folders. For the first one, you may look at the help. After each step, write why that step is right. For the second one, try it on your own first. Check the help only after you answer. Show your work for both. Then say which step felt hardest. Everything you need is printed in activity_setup. It has the exact case, what should happen, how to try it, checks, and a paper choice worth the same score. Do not wait for another handout or app. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about files and folders. It is part of "Computing Systems, Files, and Troubleshooting". Later days in this unit cover other things, like hardware and software. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about files and folders; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 5, finish on your own. Write a reason for each main choice. If there were two ways to do it, say which one you picked and why.

concept_teaching.title: Follow evidence across a system boundary: files and folders
concept_teaching.entry_check: Before reading, write one prediction about files and folders and one observation that could show the prediction is wrong. This readiness record is no-penalty evidence.
explanation: files and folders is about making a clear choice and showing why it works. First name what the result should do. Then point to the step, label, or fact that supports your choice.
A check is different from a guess. Write what you expect before you try it. Compare what happened with what you expected. If they differ, circle the first place they stop matching.
A fix needs a reason. Change one thing that your evidence supports, try the same checks again, and keep the old and new work. That record shows your thinking even when the first try was wrong.

Trace input, processing, storage, and output in order. Locate the first boundary whose observed state differs from its specified state before proposing a repair. You may use paper, objects, labelled drawings, or precise steps when a computer is not the best tool.

key_terms.definition: A named part with a defined responsibility.
The information a component holds at a particular moment.
The boundary where one component sends or receives information.
Using observations to narrow a failure to the smallest supported location.

annotations.reasoning: The input, processing, and storage observations match their specifications.
The first mismatch appears at the output boundary, so replacing storage is unsupported.
Revise the output state source so it reads the stored name.
Rerun normal save, renamed save, and empty-name rejection checks.
The log isolates a boundary but cannot prove the internal cause without an implementation trace.

debugging_reasoning.title: Use the six-move evidence cycle
required_moves: Symptom: record expected versus actual without explaining it away.
Hypothesis: state one falsifiable cause about the claim or design state before revising.
Inspection: identify the first trace row or printed detail that bears on the hypothesis.
Predicted effect: state what one controlled change should alter and what it should leave unchanged.
Test and interpretation: compare actual with the prediction and mark the hypothesis supported, rejected, or not fully tested.
Verification: rerun all relevant checks and record any new limitation or next hypothesis.
debugging_reasoning.anti_guessing_rule: A working final artifact without a pre-change hypothesis and inspectable evidence is incomplete debugging/revision evidence.

remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Copy each printed fact onto a separate card. Draw an arrow from a fact to a claim only when the fact would make that claim more or less credible. Unconnected claims must be revised or removed.
remediation_routes.analogue_task: Use four new cards about a fictional library sign to build a fact → claim → check map for files and folders; do not use the protected case.
remediation_routes.return_check: Complete the fresh mastery check with teaching materials closed. The original protected solution remains withheld.

remediation_routes.learner_signal: I changed or chose something before recording the mismatch and a testable reason.
remediation_routes.title: Different routine: the six-box evidence ladder
remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Use six boxes in order: expected/actual, first divergence or decisive detail, hypothesis, predicted effect, one revision, rerun interpretation. Do not enter the revision box until the first four constrain what the change is meant to test.
remediation_routes.analogue_task: Apply the six boxes to a separate fictional clock-card mismatch related to files and folders. Stop after the prediction, explain what result would reject the hypothesis, then finish the check.
remediation_routes.return_check: Complete the fresh mastery check independently. A correct but low-confidence response receives confirmation tied to evidence, not automatic reteaching.

guided_scaffold_note: Scaffolding for files and folders fades within the session: the first case may be worked with the reference, model, or prompts in view, and the second must be attempted before checking anything. The supporting adult may ask "what supports that move?" after a step but should not supply the step. Where the unscaffolded attempt diverges from the scaffolded one, the divergence itself is the thing to examine, not something to erase.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.

remediation: Reteaching for files and folders follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for files and folders, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for files and folders works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of files and folders, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking files and folders mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply files and folders under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on files and folders rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
